Hegemony

/hih-JEM-uh-nee/ - the stress falls on JEM · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Hegemony means the controlling dominance of one power over the rest.

Nobody voted for English's hegemony over the sciences; laboratories in forty countries simply stopped publishing in anything else.

Worked Example

Nine of every ten questions typed anywhere on earth pass through one company's search box. It owns none of the newspapers, none of the shops, none of the encyclopedias it points to — and yet headlines are rewritten to please its ranking, storefronts redesign themselves for its crawler, and a page it cannot find might as well not have been written.

Hegemony is the exact word for that position, because hegemony means the controlling dominance of one power over the rest — dominance, not ownership. A monopoly would have to own the market it rules; a hegemon rules markets it never bought, because everyone else has arranged their business around its lead.

How Hegemony Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

dominance

dominance: the plain word for being on top; hegemony adds that the others steer by your lead

supremacy

supremacy: the title for top rank; hegemony is the working arrangement that enforces it

Antonyms

rivalry

rivalry: a contest still undecided — nobody yet sets the terms

equal footing

equal footing: powers facing each other at the same height

How Strong Is It? — leverage → hegemony → empire

leverage vs. hegemony

leverage vs. hegemony: Leverage is strength for one negotiation — a good hand in a single game, spent when the deal closes.

empire vs. hegemony

empire vs. hegemony: Empire goes further than hegemony — the hegemon's rivals keep their own flags and follow its lead; an empire hauls the flags down and rules directly.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of hegemony.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — hegemon

Root — hegemon: leader, guide (Greek hegemon)

Suffix — -y

Suffix — -y: the state or condition of

Put it together

Put it together: Hegemon (leader) + -y (the condition of) = the condition of being the leader. Greek cities used hegemonia for the city that led an alliance — Athens held it, then lost it — and the word still means exactly that: not owning the others, but leading them so firmly that following becomes their habit.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Greek hegemon, the leader, produced hegemony and its adjective hegemonic — and then stopped. No everyday English word shares the root, so anchor the meaning to the picture instead: one flag out front, and the rest of the fleet steering by it.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / academic

Hegemony belongs to history seminars and foreign-affairs columns: one power, many followers, no purchase receipt. Dominance is the everyday word; supremacy the trophy word. Inside this unit, keep the lanes: centralization gathers control within one system, a despot is one person holding it, and hegemony is one power towering over its supposed equals.
